headline: Highest risk is medium: Dify can write/read shared workspace state while the paired source-available prompt-leak corpus may be treated as content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and ingest uploaded knowledge-base files, so if system_prompts_leaks content is placed in a shared workspace or fed into Dify, prompt-like text could be treated as instructions. The second agent is a source-available prompt-leak corpus with no runtime protections, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks content is copied into a Dify knowledge-base file or prompt input, THEN instruction-like text can influence downstream agent behavior.
IF Dify workflows parse uploaded text as trusted instructions, THEN prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different workspaces.
Disable ingestion of untrusted text into Dify knowledge bases.
Add a manual review step before any file becomes agent context.
Prefix all imported corpus text as data, not instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for every retrieved snippet.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, and its shared state is via Dify server datastore; if the prompt-leak corpus is stored there or reused across instances, sensitive conversation content can leak between agents. The second agent has no egress, which limits exfiltration, but the shared datastore still creates a plausible leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same Dify datastore or workspace, THEN conversation logs or knowledge-base content can be exposed across instances.
IF system_prompts_leaks is imported into shared storage, THEN its contents may be surfaced in Dify outputs.
mitigations: Use separate datastores for each agent.
Restrict Dify workspace permissions to one operator role.
Remove sensitive logs from shared storage before import.
Audit retrieval outputs for cross-agent contamination.
requires-engineering: enforce tenant isolation at the datastore layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad network egress plus filesystem write, while the second agent is non-networked and source-available; if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, Dify can overwrite or race on shared files even though the second agent cannot write back. Uncertainty about the second agent's runtime is limited, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory, THEN Dify can overwrite files the other agent expects to remain stable.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, THEN concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Turn off shared-state reuse for the pair.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs from tools and knowledge-base content, and the prompt-leak corpus can supply misleading or adversarial text. If B consumes Dify output as authoritative, errors can cascade into later actions; the second agent has no verification mechanism shown, so the pathway is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF B treats Dify output as authoritative, THEN incorrect facts can propagate without verification.
IF Dify retrieves adversarial corpus text, THEN downstream actions may be based on false premises.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Dify outputs.
Add a verification step that cross-checks retrieved facts.
Limit Dify to draft-only outputs.
Log source citations for every claim.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and model-provider API keys, so compliance risk exists if the paired corpus contains regulated data. The second agent is source-available and non-networked, so it is not the main residency risk; the concern is mainly Dify's handling of stored content and logs.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files, THEN retention and residency controls must be validated.
IF the prompt-leak corpus contains third-party confidential material, THEN redistribution may violate policy.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Dify logs.
Review retention settings before import.
Redact secrets from knowledge-base files.
Confirm data-processing terms for any external model provider.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
